hook.line: If you're not using Claude Code right now, you might be getting left behind.
hook.visual: Close selfie holding a lav mic, white 'how i would learn claude code from scratch' title top and a Claude logo sticker at the bottom.

beats.what: Fear-of-falling-behind callout to camera with title and Claude logo sticker
'*with FREE resources!' tag pops in next to the title as she says 'don't panic'
Cut to a closer framing; pixel-style 'CLAUDE CODE' sticker replaces the logo
Cut to her laptop: resource one, a YouTube crash course
Resource two: free course website shown on the laptop
Resource three: a long tutorial thread on X, scrolled on screen
Back to her face: 'and finally, if you want to go a bit deeper'
Resource four: official course page with a video player
Back to selfie for reassurance and a 'follow & comment code' title

why_it_works: FOMO line at 0 s followed by 'don't panic, it's easy' at 2.6 s: threat then relief keeps the anxious viewer
Ordered 'first / then / after that / finally' list maps progress so viewers wait for the last resource
Each resource is shown as a real page on her own laptop, which reads as a trusted personal recommendation
Comment-to-get-links CTA gives a reason to comment instead of just saving
weaknesses: 5.6 words/s is very fast; captions change faster than they can be read
Laptop screens are filmed off-screen at an angle, so page text is unreadable
Video ends mid-sentence before the CTA finishes
for_robert: Pair a fear line with an immediate 'don't panic' in the first 3 s; Fred could deliver the panic and Robert the calm answer.
